items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I studied with an uncle of mine... His names was Anton Rovinsky. And I learned a lot of things from him.

ctx.x: Yeah. In your early career, you were, when we listen to you play, we can tell that you had some classical training.

Yeah. I studied with an uncle of mine, other teachers too, but finally I was proficient enough to study with an uncle of mine who was a concert pianist. His names was Anton Rovinsky. And I learned a lot of things from him. I’m still learning from him actually, in a sense.
But to do studio work like that it’s obvious that you had to be able to sight read and do things in a short time.
